newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Bombing raid on Kabul kills 7, wounds 12.
newsitem.headline: Bombing raid on Kabul kills 7, wounds 12.

text.p: An air raid on the Afghan capital Kabul on Sunday afternoon killed at least seven people and wounded 12, residents said.
"Most of the dead and wounded came from a house where the owner was hosting a lunch for his friends and relatives," said an onlooker.

A single plane dropped bombs that hit a two-storey house in the residential Khair Khana district of northwestern Kabul, close to the airport which is used for both military and civilian traffic and has been frequently targeted in the past.

A military alliance fighting the Taleban movement which controls more than three quarters of Afghanistan, including the capital, claimed on Sunday it had pushed back the purist Islamic warriors, capturing the strategic town of Charikar and a nearby airbase.
The Taleban briefly captured most of the opposition-held north of the country in May but have since been gradually losing ground.
Relatives and neighbours dug through rubble shortly after the bombing raid looking for survivors. They said that at least seven people had been killed and 12 wounded.
Taleban guns opened up with anti-aircraft fire as the plane flew over the capital.
The raid was one of three within 24 hours. Early on Sunday morning a plane dropped at least three bombs near the airport.

"The air raid did not hit inside the airport perimeter. Two or three bombs landed close to the residential area north of here, but there are no reports of casualties," said Faizullah, head of military security at the airport.
On Sunday night, a plane dropped at least two bombs but there were no immediate reports of casualties.
The International Committee of the Red Cross and the United Nations use the airport to transport staff and supplies and had planes that landed between raids.

A senior opposition commander told Reuters on Sunday morning that their forces had captured the town of Charikar, 40 miles (64 km) north of Kabul, on Saturday night as well as the nearby Bagram airbase.
The commander, who preferred to remain anonymous, said 500 Taleban fighters had been killed.
A Taleban spokesman confirmed the loss of Charikar but denied that Bagram had fallen. There was no independent information on the situation.
Bagram was Kabul's main military airfield but has been out of action for 10 months as it was too close to the front line.
